candidates.name: Sant'Antonio Taumaturgo
candidates.content: Church of Sant’Antonio Taumaturgo in Trieste is a grand Neoclassical church dominating the end of the city’s Grand Canal. Built between 1825 and 1849 to a design by the architect Pietro Nobile, it is the largest Catholic church in

candidates.name: Museo Revoltella
candidates.content: This museum was donated to the city in 1869 by Baron Pasquale Revoltella, a great patron of the arts who liked to surround himself with precious and avant-garde works. In a building restored and extended by architect Carlo Scarpa,

candidates.name: Museo di Storia Naturale
candidates.content: Zoological, botanical, geological, palaeontological and mineralogical collections. Vivarium. Specialised scientific library..

candidates.name: Museo della Comunità Ebraica di Trieste "Carlo e Vera Wagner"
candidates.alt: "Carlo e Vera Wagner" Museum of the Jewish Community of Trieste
candidates.content: Collection of ritual art of the Jewish community of Trieste, mainly silverware and fabrics.

candidates.name: Museo della Risiera di San Sabba
candidates.content: A national monument, a testimonial of the only Nazi extermination camp in Italy.

candidates.name: Il Faro della Vittoria
candidates.content: An impressive work of the Triestine architect Arduino Berlam (1880-1946) and of the sculptor Giovanni Mayer (1863-1943), has two important functions. Besides lighting the gulf of Trieste, in order to help navigation, it also serve

candidates.name: Museo di Storia, Arte e Orto Lapidario
candidates.alt: Museum of History and Art and Lapidary Garden
candidates.content: Archaeological, historical and art collections. Prehistoric and protohuman findings of local origin; Roman and medieval sculptures and epigraphs. Egyptian, Greek, Roman and pre-Roman antiques. Numismatic collection. Photograph and

candidates.name: Città Vecchia
candidates.content: Trieste boasts an extensive old town: there are many very narrow and crooked streets with typical medieval houses. Nearly the entire area is closed to traffic.

candidates.name: The Austrian Quarter
candidates.content: Half of the city was built under Austrian-Hungarian dominion, so there are a lot of palaces that resemble Vienna. An iconic place of this quarter is the majestic Piazza Unità (Unity Square), which is Europe's largest sea-front squ

candidates.name: San Giusto Cathedral and Castle
candidates.content: A walk on the castle ramparts and bastions gives a complete panorama of the city of Trieste, its hills and the sea. It was built between the 15th and 17th centuries by the Habsburgs to control and defend the city. Its thick walls

candidates.name: The Roman Theatre
candidates.content: Tergeste, which probably dates back to the prehistoric period, was enclosed by walls built in 33-32 BC on Emperor Octavius’s orders. The city developed greatly during the 1st and 2nd century AD. The Roman Theatre faces the sea. Th

candidates.name: Museo Sartorio
candidates.content: Art collections donated to the city by the Sartorio family. Paintings from the 19th and 20th centuries; sculptures; sketches by Giambattista Tiepolo.

candidates.name: Museo della Bora
candidates.content: A small museum dedicated to Bora and wind in Trieste.

candidates.name: Grotta Gigante
candidates.content: This giant cave claims to be the biggest tourist cave in the world (since 1997 in the Guinness Book of Records). The enormous hall is 107 m high, 280 m long and 65 m wide. The multi-lingual guided tour takes about 45 minutes. You

candidates.name: Synagogue of Trieste
candidates.content: It's one of the largest in Europe, and was built in 1912. Guided tours only.

candidates.name: Miramare Castle
candidates.content: This historic 19th-century castle is a 20-minute trip from Piazza Oberdan on the #6 bus.

candidates.name: Arco di Riccardo
candidates.content: An Augustan gate built in the Roman walls in 33 AD, in the narrow streets of the old town.

candidates.name: Railway Museum Trieste Campo Marzio
candidates.content: Features drawings, models and fullsized train engines and railcars as well as horse-drawn trams from Trieste's past.

candidates.name: Saint Spyridon Church
candidates.alt: Serbian Orthodox Church of St. Spyridon

candidates.name: Roman Forum
candidates.content: The heart of the ancient city of Tergeste. Although only fragmentary remains of the Roman Forum survive—mainly paving, columns, and foundations—the site marks the civic and religious core of Tergeste.

candidates.name: Canal Grande
candidates.content: Trieste's beautiful grand canal. Step onto the bridge to pose with a bronze statue of James Joyce, one of Trieste's many iconic statues that walk the streets instead of standing on pedestals.

candidates.name: Lapidary Garden
candidates.content: Contains Roman and Medieval relics, and a cenotaph to the archaeologist Johann Winckelmann, father of neoclassicism, who died in Trieste in 1769.

candidates.name: Sailing with Discover Friuli
candidates.content: This tour agency offers half-day and full-day sailboat cruises around the Gulf of Trieste, with great views of Duino, Miramare, and the surrounding landscape from the sea.

candidates.name: The Karst
candidates.alt: Kras in Slovene, Carso in Italian
candidates.content: The limestone plateau above the city on both sides of the border. It is ideal for walking and offers excellent views of the Gulf of Trieste, coastal areas of Slovenia, and northern Croatia. Many of the villages in the Karst are ma

candidates.name: Strada Vicentina
candidates.content: A pedestrian road stretching from Opicina to Prosecco, about 6km long. The views are superb.

candidates.name: Barcola
candidates.content: Trieste's concrete, sandless beach just south of Miramare. You can sunbathe here.

candidates.name: Molo Audace
candidates.content: The long pier across from Piazza Unica d'Italia. An amazing place to relax and watch the sunset.

candidates.name: Snorkeling in Miramare
candidates.content: From the Marine Biodiversity Centre, BioMA arranges diving and snorkeling activities in the Miramare Marine Protected Area and around Gulf of Trieste.

candidates.name: Caffè San Marco
candidates.content: Open since 1914, San Marco is as popular with today's students and tourists as it was in the days of Saba and Giotti.

candidates.name: Caffè Pasticceria Pirona
candidates.content: One of the few remaining petesserias (cake shop that also sells coffee and liqueur, as well as beverages made from) to have retained its Viennese charm. One of its most devoted customers was none other than James Joyce.

candidates.name: Caffè Torinese
candidates.content: Perfectly preserved gem from the 19th century.

candidates.name: Chocolat
candidates.content: It's a must for hot chocolate in wintertime and chocolate icecream in summertime.

candidates.name: Trattoria Alla Gioconda
candidates.content: Family owned trattoria with fresh fish traditionally prepared. Genuine dishes, seasoned with the simplicity of the past to enhance the natural flavor. Generous portions. The owner is very kind. Very casual and optimal quality-to-p

candidates.name: La Pizza di Cittavecchia Trieste
candidates.content: Great pizza and friendly, The service efficient. It's nice to get away from the crowds outside and find this place with a more local feel.

candidates.name: Buffet da Siora Rosa
candidates.content: One of Trieste's oldest family-owned restaurants operating since before World War II, serving typical Triestine cuisine. Particularly famous for their proscuitto cotto: cooked ham served with piquant mustard and horseradish.

candidates.name: Pizzeria la Napa XXX Ottobre
candidates.content: Great place for a quick stop for pizza. Excellent pizza mainly take away but there are a few tables to eat it also on site. There are two types of dough, you should try them. Closed Sundays.

candidates.name: Desideri e Auguri Da Marino's
candidates.content: Excellent little Italian restaurant. The food is like homemade. The best place to have a good meal with dishes that are as alternative as they are delicious. Very friendly owner, quiet and welcoming environment.

candidates.name: Orange-ini
candidates.content: Great for a quick lunch a stone's throw from the square. Arancine are good and have a lot of variety of ingredients. Amazing cannoli freshly prepared. Very informal environment suitable for a quick lunch or a night snack. Possible

candidates.name: La Piadineria
candidates.content: Quick place to stop in and get some relatively healthy food. Outdoor seating is available. The piadina dough is very good. Good ingredients in general. Excellent choice of flavors. There is another branch of La Piadineria in Via d

candidates.name: Trattoria Citta Di Pisino
candidates.content: Trattoria with a characteristic atmosphere, with home cooking, simple but good dishes, fast service. Cucinadomaca is recommended. As soon as you enter, you are catapulted 60/70 years back, typical Triestine cuisine in a vintage se

candidates.name: Antica Trattoria Le Barettine
candidates.content: Italian seafood restaurant, huge wine collection, in Trieste's historical city center.

candidates.name: La Caveja
candidates.content: Chain serving a good selection of wraps. The best piadina! Big portions and nice ambiance in the street.

candidates.name: Marina Turkish Kebab e Pizza
candidates.content: Excellent food and service. Friendly, nice and yummy.

candidates.name: Al Barattolo
candidates.content: Considering that this restaurant is right at the Grand Canale, it has very moderate prices (and of course a beautiful view).

december.text: Other nearby airports (less than 2 hours from Trieste by private or public transport) include Ljubljana (Slovenia), and Pula & Rijeka (both in Croatia). The more adventurous and leisurely travelers can also use Zagreb Airport (Croatia), Klagenfurt (Austria), and Verona (Italy), all of which can be reached by car.
